name: Dal Makhani
description: Velvety black urad and rajma, slow-cooked to buttery perfection in 25 minutes.
steps: Soak urad and rajma overnight; drain and add to the cooker with 4 cups water and salt.
Pressure-cook on high for 8 whistles, then simmer on low for 10 minutes. Let pressure release naturally.
In the open pan, melt butter; sauté ginger-garlic, chilli and tomato purée until glossy.
Mash the dal lightly, stir it into the masala, and simmer 15 minutes — the Triply base keeps it from catching.
Finish with cream, kasuri methi and a final knob of butter.

name: Hyderabadi Dum Biryani
description: Saffron-kissed basmati layered over spiced, slow-marinated chicken and crisp birista — sealed and finished on dum.
steps: Marinate chicken in curd, ginger-garlic, biryani masala, mint and half the birista for at least 1 hour.
Heat ghee in the cooker, add whole spices, then the marinade; cook 8 minutes on medium.
Layer par-boiled basmati on top with saffron milk, ghee and the remaining birista.
Close the lid and cook for exactly 1 whistle on low, then rest 10 minutes on dum before opening.
Fluff gently from the sides and serve with mirchi ka salan and raita.

name: Punjabi Rajma Chawal
description: Kidney beans in a thick onion-tomato gravy — the Sunday lunch that tastes like home.
steps: Soak rajma overnight; pressure-cook with salt for 6 whistles until creamy.
Sauté onions in ghee until deep golden, add ginger-garlic and tomatoes.
Cook the masala until the ghee separates, then add rajma with its stock.
Simmer 10 minutes, mashing a few beans to thicken. Serve over steamed rice.

name: Moong Dal Khichdi
description: Soft, soothing rice and lentils tempered with ghee, cumin and a pinch of hing.
steps: Rinse rice and dal together.
Heat ghee, crackle cumin and hing, add rice, dal and turmeric.
Add 4 cups water and salt; cook 3 whistles. Serve with ghee, papad and pickle.

name: Kanda Poha
description: Flattened rice tossed with onion, peanuts, curry leaves and lime — ready in 15.
steps: Rinse poha and drain; season with salt, sugar and turmeric.
In the Tasra, roast peanuts, then splutter mustard and curry leaves.
Add onion until translucent, toss in poha on low heat for 3 minutes.
Finish with lime, coriander and a shower of sev.

name: Aloo Jeera Sabzi
description: Golden potatoes crisped with cumin — the deep Tasra means no spills when you toss.
steps: Heat oil in the Tasra; add cumin and chillies.
Add cubed potatoes, turmeric and salt; toss on high heat.
Finish with amchur and coriander.

name: Atta for Soft Rotis
description: The Tasra doubles as a kneading bowl — rivet-free, so dough never sticks in corners.
steps: Add salt to atta in the Tasra.
Add water gradually and knead into a soft dough.
Coat with oil, cover and rest 20 minutes.

name: Masala Chai
description: Ginger, cardamom and strong leaf — the Triply base boils milk evenly without scorching.
steps: Boil water with crushed ginger and cardamom in the Top.
Add tea leaves and sugar; simmer 2 minutes.
Add milk, bring to a rolling boil twice, strain and serve.

name: Kesar Kheer
description: Slow-reduced milk, rice and saffron — no stirring marathon thanks to even heat.
steps: Bring milk to a boil in the Top; add soaked rice.
Simmer on low for 40 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add sugar, saffron and cardamom; garnish with nuts.

name: Gujarati Kadhi
description: Silky sweet-sour yoghurt curry tempered with cloves and curry leaves.
steps: Whisk curd, besan and water in the Top until smooth.
Simmer, stirring, until it thickens slightly.
Pour over a ghee tempering of cloves, cumin and curry leaves.

name: Phulka Roti
description: The concave Pride Tawa cradles each roti so it puffs up perfectly, every time.
steps: Roll dough balls into thin discs.
Cook on the hot tawa until bubbles appear; flip.
Puff directly over the flame and brush with ghee.

name: Aloo Paratha
description: Crisp, flaky and stuffed with spiced potato — golden on a non-reactive surface.
steps: Mash potatoes with spices.
Stuff into dough, seal and roll gently.
Cook with butter until golden spots appear on both sides.

name: Masala Dosa
description: Thin, lacy and crisp — even heat across all 250 mm for restaurant-style dosas.
steps: Spread a ladle of batter thinly on the hot tawa.
Drizzle ghee and cook until crisp.
Fill with potato masala and fold.
